Straight Heavy Sets.scheme: Programmed heavy sets with full normal rest.
Straight Heavy Sets.why: Best baseline when the goal is clean, repeatable force production without extra complexity.

Top Set + Back-Offs.scheme: First work set = heaviest quality set; remaining sets = lighter back-off work.
Top Set + Back-Offs.why: Combines a high-force exposure with useful volume while avoiding repeated all-out heavy sets.

Cluster Sets.scheme: Break the prescribed reps into small clusters such as 2+2+2 with ~15–30 sec inside the set.
Cluster Sets.why: Lets you accumulate more high-quality reps with a heavy load while protecting rep speed and technique.

Heavy Primer + Work Sets.scheme: Optional crisp heavy single before the programmed work sets; keep ~2–3 RIR and never grind.
Heavy Primer + Work Sets.why: Provides a heavier exposure without turning the session into max testing; the primer is logged separately from progression work.

Primer + Paused Top/Back-Offs.scheme: One crisp heavy single @ ~2–3 RIR → full rest → paused top set → 1–2 lighter paused back-off sets.
Primer + Paused Top/Back-Offs.why: Separates exposure, performance and volume: the primer rehearses heavy load, the paused top set is the main performance set, and back-offs add quality volume.

Paused Reps.scheme: Use a deliberate pause at the programmed weak/starting position, then accelerate with control.
Paused Reps.why: Removes momentum and develops force from a stable position while improving technique under load.

Wave Loading.scheme: Build intensity across a small wave, reset, then repeat slightly heavier when the full template supports enough exposures.
Wave Loading.why: Repeated climbs can provide heavy practice without making every rep a maximal effort. Do not add sets automatically.

Dead-Stop / Pin Work.scheme: Each rep begins from a true stop or pins; no bounce or stored momentum.
Dead-Stop / Pin Work.why: Targets force production from a specific position and can address a known sticking point.

Speed / Dynamic Work.scheme: Submaximal load, perfect positions, maximal safe intent to accelerate every rep.
Speed / Dynamic Work.why: Trains rate of force development. Stop when speed or technique clearly deteriorates.

Rep-PR Set.scheme: One designated set may pursue a clean rep best while preserving ~1 RIR; no ugly grinders.
Rep-PR Set.why: Creates a repeatable performance benchmark without requiring a 1RM test.

Density Progression.scheme: Keep load/work stable and gradually complete the same quality work with less recovery.
Density Progression.why: Builds repeatable strength and work capacity; useful when density itself is the goal.

Load / Distance Progression.scheme: For carries: first increase clean load or distance/time, then use density only as an optional secondary challenge.
Load / Distance Progression.why: Matches the real goal of loaded movement, grip and trunk strength better than chasing shorter rests as the primary progression.
